text:
maria_supp: FYI customer reporting repeated streaming failures, looks like sudden socket close mid-response. Request-id: req_0a7f3c.

jasmine_customer: Hey, got a 502 and then client shows "write EPIPE" in our node logs. Happens ~35s into stream. Happened twice in last hour.

carlos_support: Can you paste the full client stack trace and the sample payload size? also which model/route?

jasmine_customer: Using hosted /v1/generate chat, model: redwood/gpt-large, prompt ~1.2k tokens, response target ~2.5k tokens. Node fetch send loop shows: 

```
FetchError: network error
 at ClientRequest.request.on (/app/node_modules/node-fetch/lib/index.js:xxx)
 error: write EPIPE
```

maria_supp: From gateway logs I see upstream closed with FIN before trailer: gateway logs: "upstream prematurely closed connection (client half-close)" for req_0a7f3c, upstream 10.22.5.18:443. Proxy returned 502.

kevin_sre: Sharing a slice of gateway debug: 

```
[2026-03-16T14:12:17.123Z] req=req_0a7f3c route=/v1/generate method=POST upstream=10.22.5.18:443 state=streaming tokens_emitted=412 last_chunk_offset=16384 socket_event=halfclose
[2026-03-16T14:12:17.124Z] upstream: write error: broken pipe (EPIPE)
[2026-03-16T14:12:17.125Z] classification: upstream-closed -> gateway-502
```

lee_eng: Do we have TLS renegotiation or keepalive timeouts between gateway and serving runtime? Could be nat timeout closing the socket mid-stream.

kevin_sre: Keepalives are 90s. This happens ~35s in so not keepalive. Possible client triggered half-close and our heuristics mark that as upstream error -> counted as 5xx. We should double-check our EOF classification.

carlos_support: Customer is worried about billing — they say these are counted as 5xx and not retriable, skipping token billing? Jasmine, do you see any billing spikes?

jasmine_customer: We got an unexpected error line in billing alerts — some streams were flagged 5xx and tokens refunded, causing credit churn. We're trying to reproduce.

maria_supp: Repro steps request: can you run a raw curl that streams chunked and then client-side abort mid-stream? That would help replicate. Example we sent: 

```
# server side: simulate streaming response; client abort after 35s
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"...","stream":true}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
# in node: setTimeout(() => req.destroy(), 35000)
```

kevin_sre: I instrumented a local repro by aborting the request from client after 36s. Gateway logs show "client halfclose" event, but we then map to 502. We need to update classification: if client closes before receiving final chunk trailer, and upstream didn't write an error, mark as client-abort not 5xx.

lee_eng: Agreed. Short-term mitigation: whitelist this route in metering to not count as server 5xx while we push a classification fix. Long-term: tweak proxy EOF handling: treat ECONNRESET/EPIPE from write after client FIN as non-failure.

maria_supp: Action items: 
- kevin_sre: create a draft change to gateway EOF handling and a unit test replicating client-side abort (ETA today).
- lee_eng: add a temporary billing rule for reqs with header x-client-abort-repro to avoid refunds/spikes (ETA tomorrow).
- carlos_support: coordinate with customer and request a small repro script run in their environment.

ops-bot: Deployment window requested: canary rollback safe path ready for gateway change? :gear:

kevin_sre: I'll open PR with tests and request canary deploy. Rolling canary to 5% first. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/3214

carlos_support: Jasmine — can you run the small node script and paste logs once done? we'll attach to ticket.

jasmine_customer: Running now, will paste within 10 mins. Thanks all. :pray:

maria_supp: Note: also verify chunked encoding trailers are honored. There have been intermittent cases where proxy stripped the trailer and then treated as premature EOF.

kevin_sre: Filed incident task: GATE-1198. I'll include sample trace for req_0a7f3c and the local repro traces.

jasmine_customer: Ran repro, logs attached — I can reproduce reliably by destroying socket at 35-37s. No server error logged, just client write EPIPE.

lee_eng: OK will prepare patch to classification logic and add metrics dimension "client_abort_detected".

maria_supp: Thanks team, keeping this open until patch is in canary and customer confirms billing no longer misclassified.

carlos_support: Closing loop: jasmine, if you see another occurrence after our patch, ping me and we'll escalate to Dedicated team.

jasmine_customer: Will do. Appreciate the quick triage everyone! :+1:
